title: Every app launch blocks the data sidecar behind two slow MCP binds (24-34s+), and the named fix (--onedir) is still not taken
repro: design + measured: launch the packaged app cold (after reboot). lib.rs setup spawns openbb-mcp + sec-edgar-mcp, JOINS both bind waits (measured 34.2s/33.6s cold in isolation, 13.6s/24.6s warm; up to 90s each under contention), and only then calls start_main_sidecar. The UI sits 'disconnected' for that whole window; if sec-edgar overruns 90s it is unavailable for the session (/sec -> 501).
notes: Covers INT-DF-1/2/22/24. A stranger's first minute of a public 0.9.0 is a dead cockpit; the wait budget hides a startup-latency defect instead of removing it. Two fix shapes, smallest first: (1) do not join the MCP threads before start_main_sidecar — spawn main sidecar immediately and hand it the MCP ports lazily (env var is read once at import in openbb_mcp_provider.py:131-141, so switch that to a late-resolved port file / Tauri command) so the terminal is usable in seconds and MCP attaches when it binds; (2) the operator-attended --onedir conversion (Tier-1 tauri.conf.json externalBin -> resources + Rust inner-exe path + one full tauri build). (1) is not Tier-1 and also fixes INT-DF-22's 'late bind is lost for the session'.

title: The openbb-mcp/sec-edgar-mcp 'deadlock fix' is a spawn-mechanism side-step, never a transport-level root-cause fix, and its production-build efficacy is unproven
repro: design: src-tauri/src/openbb_mcp.rs replaces Python subprocess.Popen with Tauri's app.shell().sidecar() spawn (side-steps the anyio/_MEIPASS/handle-inheritance deadlock class per CLAUDE.md's own gotcha) but never touches the openbb-mcp-server / sec-edgar-mcp streamable-http transport itself; BLOCKERS.md:159-177 reclassifies the residual as slow cold bind + disk contention, which is what INT-DF-1/2/22/24 already cover. Separately, the 'workflow+backtest chain actually unblocked' claim (DF-17) is only evidenced by dev-built-binary smoke tests (scripts/smoke-test-sidecars.mjs) and dev-mode backtest runs (D65) — no repo evidence of a packaged `tauri build` cold boot exercising the chain.
evidence: src-tauri/src/openbb_mcp.rs:1-13, scripts/smoke-test-sidecars.mjs:810, docs/redesign/DECISIONS.md D80 (dev binaries), D65 (dev backtest parity), BLOCKERS.md:159-177
notes: Two related but distinct gaps beyond the cold-boot-latency finding (INT-deferred-0-1): (a) the streamable-http transport's own deadlock surface was never investigated/fixed, only avoided by changing who spawns the process; (b) nothing in the repo proves the fix holds on a packaged release build, only dev/smoke-test builds. Smallest fix shape: run one `tauri build` + cold-boot smoke pass on a clean machine and record the result in DECISIONS.md; upstream transport investigation stays deferred per BLOCKERS.md (already ruled out at Phase 9.5, see INT-DF-23).

title: The copilot's multi-round tool-calling loop has never been run against a real BYOK key (Anthropic, Gemini, or Ollama) — only a scripted fake provider
repro: design: sidecar/tests/test_tool_loop_e2e.py drives the full loop (tool schema sent, tool_use dispatched, result fed back, terminal-context preamble) against a _ScriptedProvider fake only. Grep across sidecar/tests for a live-key fixture, VCR cassette, or recorded live response for any of anthropic.py, gemini.py, or ollama.py's stream_chat finds none.
notes: The mocked test proves the loop's plumbing is correct but not that any real provider actually emits tool_use in the expected shape or that the adapters parse a live response correctly — this is exactly the class of bug a mock can't catch (wire-format drift, auth header shape, streaming chunk boundaries). Smallest fix shape: one operator-attended pass per provider (Settings -> AI Providers, ask a tool-triggering question, confirm a correct multi-round answer), logged in DECISIONS.md/CHANGELOG.

title: LLMProvider.stream_chat's ABC declaration ('async def -> AsyncIterator') is typed as a coroutine but every adapter implements and every caller uses it as an async generator
repro: sidecar/services/llm/base.py:83-90 declares '@abstractmethod async def stream_chat(...) -> AsyncIterator[LLMStreamEvent]'. Every concrete adapter (anthropic.py:103, gemini.py:99, groq.py:101, ollama.py:126, openai.py:656) is an async-generator function (contains 'yield' directly in its async def body). The only call site, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1434, does 'async for event in adapter.stream_chat(...)' with no 'await' before it -- correct for an async generator, but inconsistent with what the ABC's 'async def' signature would imply (call, then await the coroutine to get the iterator).
notes: Functionally harmless today because every override and the one caller agree with each other, but the ABC lies about the contract it enforces -- a new adapter written to match the ABC's literal 'async def' type (return a coroutine that resolves to an iterator, e.g. via an inner helper) would be call-site-incompatible without a type checker catching it, since no mypy run currently gates this file (no mypy config/binary found in the repo). Smallest fix: drop 'async' from the base.py declaration, matching BLOCKERS.md's own named fix, which was never applied.

title: The four macro-provider modules' PROVIDER constant is an untyped str, not narrowed to the MacroProvider Literal the model layer already defines
repro: sidecar/models/macro_extended.py:27 defines 'MacroProvider = Literal["fred","ecb","imf","world-bank"]' and uses it on MacroSeriesExtended.provider. But sidecar/services/macro/fred_provider.py:48, imf_provider.py:31, ecb_provider.py:30, world_bank_provider.py:37 each write 'PROVIDER = "<id>"' with no type annotation, so a type checker infers plain str for the constant that gets passed into the Literal-typed model field.
notes: Only the model layer got the Literal narrowing from the original audit's fix; the four provider modules' own constants were missed. Smallest fix: annotate each as 'PROVIDER: MacroProvider = "fred"' (etc.), one line per file.

title: All three Rust kill() shutdown closures still hold a MutexGuard through the whole if-let body instead of releasing it right after .take()
repro: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:510 (main sidecar exit handler), src-tauri/src/openbb_mcp.rs:188, src-tauri/src/sec_edgar_mcp.rs:185 each still write 'if let Some(child) = state.0.lock().unwrap().take() { let _ = child.kill(); }' -- the MutexGuard temporary from '.lock().unwrap()' lives for the whole if-let block (the clippy::significant_drop_in_scrutinee shape), not just for the .take() call.
notes: Low real-world blast radius (single-threaded app-exit path), but it is exactly the pattern clippy's significant_drop_in_scrutinee/significant_drop_tightening lints exist to catch, and it widens the window where a concurrent lock().unwrap() call on the same process-state mutex would block. Smallest fix (identical at all 3 sites): 'let child = state.0.lock().unwrap().take(); if let Some(child) = child { let _ = child.kill(); }'.

repro: docs/BLUEPRINT.md:735 (Use Case 2: 'AI Researcher pulls everything') and :738 (Use Case 4) say nothing about the MCP subprocess startup gap or the F1 port-bind degrade-to-yfinance/501 behavior a user can actually hit mid-flow. Separately, :235 (Module 7 'Theming engine (dark default + light option + future custom themes)') still claims a light theme option ships, though no light-theme CSS exists anywhere in styles/ (see INT-DF-19).
notes: Doc-drift only, no code change required. Smallest fix: a one-line caveat under UC2/UC4 noting the MCP-unavailable degrade path, and either strike 'light option' from Module 7 or footnote it as deferred to v1.1 (matches the S2 item 10 recommendation already on record in BLOCKERS.md).

title: Far more than the '10 fields' the original audit counted are still missing id/name attributes -- 70+ <input> elements across 40+ component files
repro: grep every '<input' tag in src/**/*.tsx (excluding tests) for a same-tag 'id=' attribute: 70+ instances across 41 files have none, e.g. src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:319-327 (a checkbox switch with an aria-label but no id/name), plus PortfolioPanel.tsx, ScreenerCriteriaBuilder.tsx, BrokerOrderEntry.tsx, OptionPricerPanel.tsx, and many more.
evidence: src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:319-327, src/modules/portfolio/PortfolioPanel.tsx, src/modules/screener/ScreenerCriteriaBuilder.tsx, src/modules/quant/OptionPricerPanel.tsx (representative sample of 41 files)
notes: Functional defect per COMMON.md's UI-findings rule (broken/incomplete form-control semantics, not visual taste): missing id/name breaks autofill, password-manager integration, and any test or automation tool that targets inputs by id. The scale (70+, not 10) means this needs a sweep, not a spot-fix -- smallest fix shape is a lint rule (eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y 'label-has-associated-control' or a custom rule) plus a batch pass, not fixing individual call sites piecemeal.

title: Settings -> Keybindings lets a user remap a shortcut, but the app-wide keydown handlers mostly ignore the remap -- only 1 of 11 defined actions is actually wired to it
repro: src/store/keybindings.ts:58-152 defines 11 remappable actions with a working store (bindingFor/setBinding/matchesEvent). But 'matchesEvent' -- the only function that consults the LIVE, possibly-remapped binding -- is imported and called in exactly one place, src/components/AgentDock.tsx:71 (agent.toggle). src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:77-83 instead hardcodes '(event.metaKey||event.ctrlKey) && event.key.toLowerCase()==="k"' directly in its own keydown listener -- remapping palette.open in Settings has no effect on the actual global handler.
evidence: src/store/keybindings.ts:58-152 (action defs), :367 (matchesEvent), src/components/AgentDock.tsx:70-71 (the one live consumer), src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:72-83 (hardcoded combo, bypasses the store)
notes: A shipped settings surface that silently doesn't do what it promises for 10 of 11 actions is a real trust defect (BLOCKERS.md flagged this as L11-keyboard-handlers-minimal but undercounted how close-yet-broken it is: the store + UI are fully built, only the wiring is missing). Smallest fix shape: route every hardcoded handler (CommandPalette and whichever others own 'their' bindings per the keybindings.ts comment at :99-102) through 'useKeybindingsStore.getState().bindingFor(actionId)' + 'matchesEvent' instead of a literal key comparison.

title: The openbb-mcp PyInstaller spec still carries a redundant --copy-metadata=fastmcp-slim entry for a package that isn't even installed
repro: scripts/ensure-openbb-mcp-sidecar.mjs:147 already does '--collect-all=fastmcp' (which bundles fastmcp's own dist-info metadata); the separate copyMeta list at :159-160 additionally does '--copy-metadata=fastmcp' (redundant with collect-all) and '--copy-metadata=fastmcp-slim'. 'sidecar/.venv/bin/pip show fastmcp-slim' returns 'WARNING: Package(s) not found: fastmcp-slim' -- it isn't in the dependency tree at all.
notes: Harmless today (PyInstaller likely just warns and skips the missing metadata target) but dead configuration that will confuse the next person auditing the build. Smallest fix: drop 'fastmcp-slim' from copyMeta and drop the redundant 'fastmcp' copy-metadata entry since collect-all already covers it.

title: vitest.config.ts has no coverage block -- 'pnpm test -- --coverage' has nothing configured to report against
repro: vitest.config.ts:1-18 (full file) -- the 'test' block has environment, globals, setupFiles, include, but no 'coverage' key (provider, thresholds, or reporters).
notes: No coverage regression gate exists for the frontend test suite. Smallest fix: add 'coverage: { provider: "v8", reporter: ["text","html"] }' (thresholds optional, add once a baseline is measured).

title: The macOS release build has no code-signing (Developer ID or notarization) configured
repro: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:30-45 (bundle block) has no macOS signingIdentity or notarization keys. docs/redesign/KEYCHAIN_DEV_SIGNING.md + scripts/macos-dev-setup.sh cover only a dev-loop ad-hoc re-signing workaround for the keychain ACL (so 'tauri dev' doesn't re-prompt every rebuild) -- not a release signing pipeline.
notes: A macOS build distributed to a stranger without Developer ID signing triggers Gatekeeper's 'unidentified developer' block on first launch -- a real first-minute defect for a public 0.9.0 release, not merely cosmetic. BLOCKERS.md already tracks this (v0.8.0->Phase 9 item 6); still open at current HEAD. Fix requires an Apple Developer ID (operator-owned credential), out of this worker's reach.
